title: Sweet Is the Light of Sabbath Eve
description: Sweet Is the Light of Sabbath Eve in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Edmeston wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 462, “Sabbath Evening”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sweet is the light of Sab-bath eve, And soft the sun-beam lin-gering there; Those sa-cred hours this low earth leave, Waft-ed on wings of praise and prayer.

lines: Sweet is the light of Sabbath eve,
And soft the sunbeam lingering there;
Those sacred hours this low earth leave,
Wafted on wings of praise and prayer.
The time, how lovely and how still!
Peace shines and smiles on all below;
The plain, the stream, the wood, the hill,
All fair with evening's setting glow!
Season of rest! the tranquil soul
Feels thy sweet calm, and melts in love;
And while these sacred moments roll,
Faith sees a smiling heaven above.
Thou God of mercy, swift to hear,
More swift than man to tell his need;
Be Thou to us, this evening, near,
And to Thy fount our spirits lead!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Edmeston died in 1867.
credits: Words by James Edmeston (1791–1867), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
